# SQL Server Database Security (DB)

These rules apply to all database scripts, stored procedures and database operations (IT-57 §8). Query parameterization in application code is covered by SCS-INP-02.

## SCS-DB-01 Parameterize stored procedures and dynamic SQL

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Stored procedures and database scripts MUST use parameters. Any dynamic SQL MUST be executed with sp_executesql and parameters, and MUST NOT be built by concatenating user input. Object names in dynamic SQL MUST be wrapped with QUOTENAME and checked against an allow-list.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- EXEC sp_executesql @sql, N'@Status nvarchar(20)', @Status = @Status; never EXEC(@sql) with concatenated values.
- Validate dynamic sort or column names against sys.columns or a fixed list, and wrap them with QUOTENAME().
- Call stored procedures from .NET with CommandType.StoredProcedure and SqlParameter objects.

Verification: Review of every stored procedure that contains EXEC( or sp_executesql. SAST/SQL linting where available.

## SCS-DB-02 Give applications least-privilege database logins

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Each application MUST connect with its own database login that has only the permissions it needs, preferably EXECUTE on its stored procedures. Applications MUST NEVER use sa, sysadmin, db_owner or any other admin account. Schema migrations MUST use a separate login from the runtime application.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Create one login/user per application and environment. Grant EXECUTE on the application schema, or db_datareader/db_datawriter or granular grants if EF Core needs table access.
- Run EF Core migrations or deployment scripts with a separate, more privileged login that is used only by the pipeline or the DBA.
- Prefer Windows integrated authentication or managed identity over SQL passwords.
- Never grant wildcard or server-level permissions to application logins.

Verification: Quarterly permission review: query sys.database_role_members and sys.server_role_members for application logins.

## SCS-DB-03 Encrypt sensitive data and connections in SQL Server

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Databases holding sensitive data MUST be encrypted at rest (TDE), and sensitive columns MUST use column-level encryption or Always Encrypted where the data classification requires it. Database connections MUST be encrypted with a validated server certificate. Passwords MUST NEVER be stored in plain text (see SCS-AUTH-02).

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Enable Transparent Data Encryption on databases with Confidential or higher data, and back up the TDE certificate securely.
- Use Always Encrypted or column-level encryption for highly sensitive fields (for example national ID, bank account).
- Connection strings: Encrypt=True (the default since Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 4.0). Never TrustServerCertificate=True; install a trusted certificate instead.
- Record which columns are encrypted in the data classification register.

Verification: Query sys.dm_database_encryption_keys for TDE status. Grep connection strings for TrustServerCertificate and Encrypt=False.

## SCS-DB-04 Keep SQL Server auditing on in production

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: SQL Server audit logging MUST be enabled on production databases for schema (DDL) changes, permission and role changes, and failed logins. Audit logging MUST NOT be disabled in production.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Create a SQL Server Audit with a server audit specification (FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP, SERVER_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUP, SERVER_PERMISSION_CHANGE_GROUP) and a database audit specification (SCHEMA_OBJECT_CHANGE_GROUP, DATABASE_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUP, DATABASE_PERMISSION_CHANGE_GROUP).
- Write audit files to a location that application logins cannot modify, and forward them to central logging where available.
- Keep audit records for the retention period set by the ISMS logging policy.

Verification: Check sys.server_audits and sys.database_audit_specifications show the audits as enabled.

## SCS-DB-05 Encrypt and protect database backups

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Database backups MUST be encrypted and stored only in locations with access control. Backup credentials and encryption keys MUST be stored securely. Unencrypted backups MUST NOT be kept on shared network locations. Production backups MUST NOT be restored into development or test environments.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Use BACKUP DATABASE ... WITH ENCRYPTION (ALGORITHM = AES_256, SERVER CERTIFICATE = ...), and back up the certificate and its private key separately.
- Restrict the backup share to the DBA and backup service accounts.
- Test restores regularly, in a controlled environment.

Verification: Check msdb.dbo.backupset for encryptor_type on production backups; review backup share permissions.
